refuted_wrong.title: Container healthcheck budgets are shorter than the cold start the same repo documents
refuted_wrong.why: The literal numbers are quoted correctly at HEAD efbbe18 (HEALTHCHECK --start-period=90s --retries=3 --interval=30s in Dockerfile; `if [ "$i" -gt 600 ]` in ops/docker-entrypoint.sh; grace_period = "120s" in fly.toml), but the premise that ties them into a defect is false. The auditor asserts the daemon backfills bars BEFORE it listens, so the real cold start is multi-minute and the 90s/120s probes cut into it. The code says the opposite: the broad-universe deep backfill (~800k bars, the "few minutes" DEPLOY.md describes) runs in `go func()` at daemon/cmd/signaldeckd/run.go:197 with the comment "The deep backfill runs in a goroutine so it never blocks daemon startup"; the watchlist seed only calls `backfiller.Enqueue(...)` (run.go:148,164), i.e. queued work, and api.Serve is reached at run.go:670. Everything synchronous before listening is local SQLite: schema creation, bootstrapUsers, symbol upserts. I measured both halves. Executing daemon/internal/store/schema.sql into a fresh temp DB creates 106 tables in 2.475s. The live daemon's own log shows boot-to-listen of ~1.4s on the multi-GB warm database. So realistic cold boot to a listening daemon is single-digit seconds, plus a prebuilt `next start`; 90s start-period and 120s Fly grace are generous, not short. The 600s in the entrypoint is a failure ceiling before giving up, not an expected duration — three numbers serving three different purposes is not three guesses at one number. The claimed impact is also weak independently: the auditor concedes plain Docker does not restart on unhealthy, and the named platforms (Railway, Render) use their own configured healthcheck path rather than the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK, so the "restart loop on first boot" needs a restart-on-unhealthy supervisor that nothing here configures. What is left is a stale comment in ops/docker-entrypoint.sh ("creates 97 tables and backfills bars before it listens", also still saying 97 where DEPLOY.md now says 105) and DEPLOY.md prose that reads as if the first-boot list is pre-serve — documentation drift, not an operational defect, and none of it touches the 7-route public surface.
